title: FoodRAG Persona-Relative Guideline Reference Tables
description: Reference nutrient bands for the Guideline Adherence metric (Evaluation Protocol Sec. 4.5.1). Persona-class based, NOT individualized, because GDPR-minimal personas lack the exact age/weight/sex/activity needed for individualized EFSA computation. Each class fixes reference anthropometrics + activity as stated modeling assumptions.
status: Researcher-constructed from authoritative public guidelines (EFSA DRV, WHO). NOT clinically validated by a nutrition specialist — see limitations. Used as a documented modeling assumption for evaluating recommendation quality, not as clinical advice.
primary_source: EFSA Dietary Reference Values (DRV), NDA Panel 2010-2019
sugar_source: WHO Guideline: Sugars intake for adults and children (2015)

modeling_assumptions.why_class_based: EFSA energy references depend on body weight, sex, age and physical activity level (PAL). Personas carry only age RANGE + condition + allergies + tags (GDPR minimization). Individualized targets would manufacture false precision. Each persona is therefore mapped to ONE reference class with fixed assumptions.
modeling_assumptions.reference_body_weight_note: Used for weight-scaled nutrients (protein at 0.83 g/kg). 70 kg is a conventional adult reference; documented assumption, not a claim about any persona.
modeling_assumptions.reference_energy_note: EFSA derives energy from REE x PAL. 2000 kcal is the conventional adult reference intake used for %-energy conversions; overridden per class where activity differs.

energy_percent_conversion.note: E% bands are converted to gram bands using the class reference energy. Example: 45-60 E% carb at 2000 kcal = 225-300 g/day.

band_semantics.within_band: Plan aggregate daily total falls inside [low, high] inclusive -> nutrient scored 1.
band_semantics.outside_band: Plan aggregate total below low OR above high -> nutrient scored 0. Record direction (under/over).
band_semantics.hard_ceiling: Where a Tolerable Upper Level (UL) or safety ceiling exists, exceeding it is flagged as a SAFETY violation (feeds Hard-Constraint Violation, Sec 4.3), not merely out-of-band.
band_semantics.as_low_as_possible: For nutrients EFSA says minimize (saturated fat, trans fat), no lower bound; a policy upper threshold is applied and documented as a non-EFSA modeling choice.

general_adult.label: General healthy adult, moderately active
general_adult.applies_to: Personas with no health condition affecting nutrition; default class

energy_kcal.source: EFSA energy DRV; +/-10% band around class reference

protein_g.source: EFSA PRI 0.83 g/kg x 70 kg = 58 g (lower); upper ~2x as generous practical ceiling
protein_g.note: Lower bound is the EFSA PRI; upper bound is a practical modeling ceiling, not an EFSA UL (none set).

saturated_fat_g.source: EFSA: 'as low as possible', no UL. High = ~10 E% policy threshold (WHO/FBDG common), documented non-EFSA choice

fibre_g.source: EFSA AI 25 g/day (lower); upper = practical high-intake benchmark
fibre_g.note: EFSA sets 25 g as adequate; higher is beneficial, so upper bound is generous.

sugars_g.source: WHO <10 E% of 2000 kcal = 50 g/day (added/free sugars). EFSA sets no UL
sugars_g.note: WHO conditional <5 E% (25 g) is a stricter optional variant.

energy_kcal.source: Same as general; energy not the primary lever

protein_g.source: EFSA PRI; no diabetes-specific change for non-nephropathy

carbohydrate_g.source: Tighter band ~40-50 E% at 2000 kcal per T1D glycemic-control evidence (PMC12440888); cf. general 45-60%
carbohydrate_g.note: CONDITION-SPECIFIC OVERRIDE. Mirrors pFoodReq's ADA-guideline precedent.

saturated_fat_g.source: As low as possible; 10 E% policy ceiling

fibre_g.source: EFSA AI 25 g; higher fibre beneficial for glycemic control, generous upper

sodium_g.source: EFSA acceptable range; tighter if comorbid hypertension (see hypertension class)

sugars_g.source: Stricter WHO conditional <5 E% = 25 g, appropriate for diabetes

hypertension_adult.label: Adult requiring reduced sodium (hypertension / cardiovascular risk)
hypertension_adult.applies_to: Personas with hypertension or explicit low-sodium requirement

saturated_fat_g.source: As low as possible; 10 E% ceiling

sodium_g.source: WHO <2 g/day sodium for hypertension/CVD; tighter than EFSA upper 3.5

energy_kcal.source: Reduced-energy reference for weight loss; ~-20% vs general
energy_kcal.note: CONDITION-SPECIFIC OVERRIDE (reduced energy). Gram bands below recomputed at 1600 kcal.

protein_g.source: Higher lower bound (satiety/lean-mass preservation); EFSA PRI floor still met

fibre_g.source: EFSA AI 25 g (not energy-scaled down; fibre benefits satiety)

persona_to_class_mapping.description: Rules mapping a persona's condition field to a reference class. Applied in priority order (first match wins). Comorbidities: see conflict_resolution.

conflict_resolution.description: If a persona matches multiple conditions (e.g., diabetic AND hypertensive), take the STRICTER band per nutrient across matched classes (min of upper bounds, max of lower bounds). Document the composite as a derived class in the run manifest.
conflict_resolution.example: diabetic + hypertension -> carbohydrate from diabetic_adult (200-250), sodium from hypertension_adult (<=2.0), sugars from diabetic_adult (<=25).

metric_computation.guideline_adherence_per_nutrient: For each tracked nutrient n: 1 if plan aggregate daily total(n) within [low, high], else 0. Record direction (under/over) when 0.
metric_computation.guideline_adherence_overall: Mean over tracked nutrients of the per-nutrient 0/1 (fraction within band). Report per-nutrient breakdown ALWAYS; overall is a summary only.
metric_computation.hard_ceiling_interaction: If total(n) > hard_ceiling(n), additionally flag a safety violation feeding Hard-Constraint Violation Rate (Sec 4.3). A nutrient can be out-of-band without being a safety violation (e.g., low fibre) but exceeding a hard_ceiling is always a safety flag.

limitations: SINGLE-DAY SNAPSHOT: dietary guidelines are framed over longer periods; a one-day plan is an approximation. State explicitly in the paper.

CLASS-BASED not individualized: reference anthropometrics (70 kg, 2000 kcal) are documented assumptions, not persona-specific measurements. Frame results as 'relative to EFSA DRV reference intakes for [class]', NOT 'meets dietary guidelines'.
SATURATED-FAT and SUGAR upper thresholds are policy choices (WHO / 10 E% convention), not EFSA ULs (EFSA sets none). Documented as non-EFSA modeling decisions.
PRACTICAL UPPER BOUNDS on protein/fibre are generous modeling ceilings where EFSA sets only a lower reference; flagged per-nutrient.

NOT CLINICALLY VALIDATED: the reference bands were constructed by the research team directly from authoritative public guidelines (EFSA DRV, WHO), without review by a nutrition specialist. This is a documented assumption and a limitation of the metric. The condition-specific override bands and the practical upper ceilings on protein/fibre (where EFSA sets only a lower reference) are the least-certain values and should be read as reasonable modeling choices, not clinical recommendations.
NOT a clinical endorsement: this is a nutrition-informational metric for evaluating recommendation quality, not medical advice.

citations.efsa_carbohydrate_fibre_2010: EFSA NDA Panel (2010). Scientific Opinion on DRVs for carbohydrates and dietary fibre. EFSA Journal 8(3):1462. (carb 45-60 E%; fibre 25 g/day)
citations.efsa_fats_2010: EFSA NDA Panel (2010). Scientific Opinion on DRVs for fats. EFSA Journal 8(3):1461. (total fat 20-35 E%; SFA as low as possible)
citations.efsa_protein_2012: EFSA NDA Panel (2012). Scientific Opinion on DRVs for protein. EFSA Journal 10(2):2557. (PRI 0.83 g/kg bw/day adults)
citations.efsa_sodium_2019: EFSA NDA Panel (2019). Dietary reference values for sodium. EFSA Journal 17(9):5778. (acceptable range 0.575-3.5 g/day adults)
citations.efsa_summary_2017: EFSA (2017). Dietary Reference Values for nutrients - Summary report. EFSA Supporting Publication e15121. (PAL values 1.4-2.0)
citations.who_sugars_2015: WHO (2015). Guideline: Sugars intake for adults and children. (<10 E% strong; <5 E% conditional)
citations.who_sodium_2012: WHO (2012). Guideline: Sodium intake for adults and children. (<2 g/day sodium)
citations.diabetes_carb_evidence: Assoc. between daily carbohydrate intake and TIR in T1D adults, PMC12440888. (40-50 E% carb for glycemic control)
